subject: USAGE clause
notes: THE DIRECT ARM -- WHICH IS ALL SR15 GOVERNS -- IS ENFORCED, AND BOTH FILE-SECTION ENTRY KINDS WERE MEASURED. `FD F. 01 R USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE.` is COBOL1725 quoting SR15 (the negative golden); a SUBORDINATE object-reference member of an FD record is caught at the member (u_sr15_sub); and an `SD S. 01 SR USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE.` sort-merge record is caught too (u_sr15_sd) -- IsFileSectionItem is the SAME AS twin's own root test, shared rather than re-written. The report is deliberately independent of SR14 (an FD record may legally be a level-1 elementary item, so SR14 admits it and only SR15 rejects it), which is what makes the golden attributable. ⚠ A SIBLING RULE OF A DIFFERENT CLAUSE IS THE ONE THAT LEAKS, AND IT WAS MEASURED HERE: the standard states this prohibition THREE times -- SR15 for the direct clause, 13.18.49.3 SR6 for SAME AS (cite --check OK; enforced as COBOL1556 since the SAME AS landing) and 13.18.57.3 SR8 for TYPE (cite --check OK: "When the TYPE clause is specified in the file section, the description of type-name-1, including its subordinate data items, shall not contain a data item described with a USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE clause"). The TYPE arm is UNENFORCED: `FD F. 01 R TYPE OT.` with `01 OT IS TYPEDEF USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE.` in WORKING-STORAGE COMPILES AND RUNS CLEAN (probe u_sr15_typeclone) -- ConformanceForest prunes the TYPE clone subtree and the template itself is a legal level-1 working-storage entry, so no arm ever looks. That is a 13.18.57.3 row, not this one; see finding usage-p1/F8. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.UsageDeclaration.cs:112-125 (CheckUsageDeclarations, the SR15 arm -- COBOL1725 over IsFileSectionItem, reported independently of SR14 so a level-1 FD record is attributed to its own rule) || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 2002,2014,2023 (USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE is post-1985)
